paper_title: WorldLatent: A Unified 4D Latent Space for World Perception and Generation

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Generative Pre-Training (GPT) represents a profound milestone in natural language processing, serving as the foundation for most of today's state-of-the-art large language models. By casting diverse understanding and generation problems into a shared token representation, GPT enables a single architecture and unified optimization loop to master heterogeneous tasks across massive corpora, giving rise to powerful foundation models for natural language. In contrast, 4D spatiotemporal vision lacks a common representational protocol: perception (such as depth and camera estimation) and generation are either handled by separate one-way pipelines or bolted together from unaligned single-modality spaces. In this work, we introduce WorldLatent, a framework that formulates a unified 4D latent space as a common protocol for both world perception and generation. Rather than relying on fragmented, task-specific models or stacked single-modality representations, our framework proposes a multimodal VAE architecture that compresses and fuses complex 4D visual appearance, geometry, and dynamics into a single structured latent representation. Within this formulation, perception and generation operate as complementary denoising processes over the same latent space, enabling one generative model to learn both capabilities simultaneously within a single training loop. Experiments across representative 4D benchmarks verify that our fused latent protocol achieves specialist-level zero-shot 4D perception, coherent 4D generation, and controllable editing from a single model. By demonstrating that diverse 4D tasks can be seamlessly unified under a shared representational protocol, our work provides a scalable foundation for general-purpose 4D spatial intelligence.

Paradigm shift toward unified 4D world modeling. (a) Prior paradigm: 4D perception and generation rely on separate one-way pipelines or unaligned, stacked modality spaces. (b) WorldLatent (Ours): Our unified 4D latent space enables single generative model and shared multi-task training loop to jointly execute 1) 4D perception (RGB 3D geometry and camera poses), 2) Text-to-4D generation (text RGB video, 3D geometry, and camera motion), and 3) Controllable 4D editing (depth + text diverse appearance-edited videos, e.g., recolored trucks). Orange borders denote target task outputs decoded from the generated full 4D latent.

Rather than relying on fragmented, task-specific models or stacked single-modality representations, our framework proposes multimodal VAE architecture that compresses and fuses complex 4D visual appearance, geometry, and dynamics into single structured latent representation. Introduction The establishment of unified task protocol in Generative Pre-Training (GPT) [5, 41, 42] marked transformative milestone in natural language processing. Rather than relying on specialized architectures and loss functions [10, 27, 48, 52] for text classification, machine translation, question answering, and open-ended synthesis, casting these diverse problems into shared token representation enabled single model to learn both understanding and generation within one optimization objective. Inspired by this success, we argue that achieving general-purpose 4D spatial intelligence in computer vision requires similar unification: an intelligent visual system must not only perceive the 3D geometry and camera motion of dynamic scene from video, but also imagine, synthesize, and edit coherent 4D worlds over time. Yet, in contrast to language modeling, 4D spatiotemporal vision still lacks such common representational protocol. As illustrated in Figure 1(a), contemporary 4D perception and video generation still rely on separate one-way pipelines or unaligned, stacked modality spaces. On the perception side, feed-forward geometric reconstructors [30, 31, 56, 58, 59, 70] and diffusion-based depth or pose estimators [19, 25, 65, 69], including recent adaptations of video generators for geometry estimation [22, 51], map videos to depth, point clouds, or camera trajectories, yet overwrite or omit RGB generation and cannot synthesize new visual worlds. On the generation side, large-scale video Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) [4, 55, 67] synthesize compelling imagery in 2D RGB latent spaces without explicit 3D grounding, geometry-guided generators [46, 61] inject external 3D caches or feature alignment unidirectionally while still decoding solely into 2D pixels. Even recent frameworks that jointly diffuse appearance and geometry within one backbone [28, 72, 78] bypass multimodal tokenizer learning, heuristically passing geometric maps through frozen RGB Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) and concatenating disjoint latents. Bridging these two paradigms properly is nontrivial: geometric estimation methods seek representations that capture high-level structural abstraction to infer scene geometry and camera motions, whereas video generation models rely on generative compression that preserves lowlevel photometric details for high-fidelity visual reconstruction. This tension between geometric abstraction and generative compression motivates learning genuinely fused representation rather than stacking separate latents. In this work, we take step toward scaling generalpurpose 4D spatial intelligence by tackling the fundamental question: How can diverse knowledge of 4D world perception and generation be consolidated into single generative model with shared multi-task training loop? Inspired by task unification in large language models, we seek shared 4D representational protocol across visual appearance, geometry, and dynamics to bridge these capabilities. To realize this protocol, we introduce WorldLatent (Figure 1(b)), framework that establishes unified 4D latent space as shared spatiotemporal representation for world perception and generation. Rather than relying on one-way pipelines or stacking unaligned modality latents, WorldLatent parameterizes dynamic scene jointly via RGB video, dense depth, and pixel-aligned camera ray maps. To reconcile geometric structure with high-fidelity appearance compression, we design multimodal 4D Variational Autoencoder (VAE) that compresses and fuses these modalities into single spatiotemporal latent grid at the same token resolution as standard video VAEs. Built upon this shared representation, WorldLatent unifies perception, generation, and controllable editing as complementary Any-to-4D denoising processes within single generative model: (1) Any-to-4D Perception (RGB Full 4D Latent), which conditions on an uncalibrated monocular video and denoises the full 4D latent to recover depth, dynamic 3D point clouds, and camera trajectories, (2) Anyto-4D Generation (Text Full 4D Latent), which jointly denoises appearance, depth, and camera rays from noise to synthesize coherent videos paired with aligned 3D scene geometry and camera motion, and (3) Any-to-4D Editing and Rendering (Depth + Text Full 4D Latent), which conditions on 4D depth structure and text prompts to render or edit visual appearance with strict 3D geometric adherence. Because every capability operates over the same latents with identical input and output spaces, generative backbone can be adapted into general-purpose 4D world model within single multi-task training loop across perception and generation. We instantiate and validate WorldLatent on 14Bparameter generative model trained jointly across 4D perception, generation, and controllable editing. Evaluating across indoor, outdoor, and dynamic 4D benchmarks (MPI Sintel [6], Bonn [40], and ScanNet [9]) as well as textto-4D and depth-guided synthesis, we show that our fused 4D latent representation enables joint multi-task denoising within single model, delivering strong geometric estimation, faithful geometry-guided rendering, and coherent 4D generation over shared input-and-output latent space. In summary, our main contributions are threefold: We propose WorldLatent, unified 4D latent protocol for world perception and generation, employing multimodal VAE to compress and fuse 4D visual appearance, geometry, and dynamics into single shared latent space for diverse downstream 4D tasks. We formulate unified Any-to-4D generative modeling 2 paradigm that consolidates 4D perception, generation, and editing into single model with shared multi-task training loop over the WorldLatent representation. Across controlled ablations and 14B-parameter unified model, we demonstrate that single generative model trained on WorldLatent effectively supports dynamic 4D perception, 4D scene generation, and controllable neural rendering, establishing scalable foundation for generalpurpose 4D spatial intelligence. 2. Related Work 3D and 4D Spatiotemporal Perception. Feed-forward pointmap regressors [30, 31, 56, 59] predict 3D point clouds without structure-from-motion, with extensions to dynamic and streaming videos [58, 70]. Meanwhile, monocular [8, 66] and diffusion [19, 25, 49] depth models recover 2.5D depth without camera poses, and video-diffusion adaptations [22, 51, 65] estimate multi-frame 3D/4D geometry. Video and 4D World Generation. Video DiTs [4, 55, 67] lack 3D grounding in RGB latents, causing static-camera bias or drift. Conditioned generators inject camera, depth, or 3D cache cues [11, 16, 46, 71], or align features to geometric teachers [61], unidirectionally without inferring 4D geometry, while dedicated 4D generators [2, 13, 32, 62, 64] remain synthesis specialists. Although WVD [72] and Aether [78] jointly diffuse appearance and geometry, WVD targets image-conditioned static scenes and Aether drops text conditioning on synthetic-only data, neither supports general-purpose multi-task learning across open-world 4D perception, generation, and editing under unified representation protocol. Unified Multi-Task Representation Protocols. Inspired by unified task protocols in NLP [42] and multimodal vision [3, 37, 38], recent works explore joint latent spaces: Orchid [29] encodes RGB, depth, and normals for static 2D images, requiring separate image-conditioned finetuning for perception, while MotionCrafter [79] learns 4D geometry-and-motion VAE without visual synthesis. In 4D world modeling, joint frameworks [28, 72, 78] heuristically stack frozen RGB-VAE and geometric channels, retaining cross-modal redundancy and rigid modality boundaries. Instead, WorldVAE fuses RGB video, depth, and camera rays into single compact bottleneck at an RGB-only VAEs token count, enabling the unification of 4D perception, generation, and editing within one model and multi-task training. 3. Method Our goal is to establish unified representational protocol that bridges 4D physical perception and generative modeling within single model and single optimization loop. As illustrated in Figure 2, our WorldLatent training pipeline consists of two stages: (a) Unified 4D Latent Space via multimodal WorldVAE training and (b) Unified Any-to-4D Generative Modeling via WorldLatent diffusion training. 3.1. WorldLatent: Unified 4D Latent Space Spatiotemporal 4D Modality Representation. dynamic 3D scene observed over frames at spatial resolution comprises visual appearance, 3D scene geometry, and camera motion. To align all modalities onto common spatiotemporal grid, we parameterize camera trajectories using dense Plucker ray coordinates [69]. For each pixel (u, v) at frame t, its camera ray is uniquely defined by unit ray direction dt,u,v R3 and ray moment mt,u,v = ot dt,u,v R3, where ot R3 denotes the camera optical center in world coordinates. Thus, any 4D scene is represented by four spatiotemporally aligned tensors: (1) Visual Appearance (RGB Video): X1 = RT HW 3, (2) Scene Geometry (4D Depth Map): X2 = RT HW 1, (3) Camera Ray Direction: X3 = RT HW 3, and (4) Camera Ray Moment: X4 = RT HW 3. Specifically, at four intermediate ViT tap depths, the four modality token streams at each spatiotemporal patch are concatenated channel-wise and projected into single fused token grid via two-layer GELU MLP [17] with LayerNorm [1]. Partial WorldLatent Encoding and Decoding. Leveraging the flexibility of our DPT token fusion mechanism, we apply random modality-level token masking during training, where unprovided modality streams are replaced with learnable mask tokens prior to fusion. This equips WorldVAE with the ability to encode and decode arbitrary subsets of input modalities into partial WorldLatent representation c4d, seamlessly bridging full-modality reconstruction in stage (a) and partial-modality conditioning in stage (b). 3.2. The results and comparisons are best viewed through video examples. We include video results in our project webpage. 4.3. Any-to-4D: 4D Perception 4.1. Experimental Setup Implementation Details. WorldVAE initializes all four encoder-decoder pairs from the Wan VAE [55], freezing the encoders while fine-tuning the decoders alongside 20Mparameter DPT Fusion module. For Any-to-4D, we finetune all parameters of Wan2.1-T2V-14B to generate 17frame, 512512 sequences across RGB, depth, and rays. Datasets. We train on 1.4M synthetic and real-world 17frame clips, using DA3-Giant [31] to label depth and camera poses on clips lacking dense 4D ground truth. Full training and dataset details in the supplementary material. 4.2. 4D WorldVAE Reconstruction Quality We first evaluate the representational capacity and computational efficiency of WorldVAE in Table 1. naive approach to joint 4D generation is to tokenize RGB, depth, and camera rays as separate latent streams, which triples the sequence length (15,360 vs. 5,120 DiT tokens) and incurs 3.84 computational overhead (569.1 vs. 148.1 TFLOPs per NFE on 14B DiT) due to quadratic self-attention scaling. In contrast, WorldVAE fuses all three modalities into single 5646432 latent grid, preserving the exact 5,120-token count of the RGB-only VAE. Because widening the latent channels from 16 to 32 only affects the initial patch-embedding and final projection layers of the DiT, WorldVAE adds negligible +0.0165% TFLOPs overhead. Despite compressing four heterogeneous 4D modalities into single compact bottleneck, WorldVAE achieves strong zero-shot round-trip reconstruction across all domains on unseen evaluation benchmarks, including MPI Sintel and the ScanNet test split: it retains high visual fidelity (32.23 dB PSNR, 0.888 SSIM) alongside accurate metric depth recovery (0.056 AbsRel, 0.984 δ1) and precise camera ray reconstruction (1.46 ray angular error, 1.77 relative rotation error). This confirms that z4d serves as compact, loss-tolerant spatial language that generalizes well for downstream Any-to-4D diffusion modeling. To evaluate how well our unified representation protocol supports physical scene understanding, we benchmark WorldLatent-14B zero-shot across three dynamic and static 4D benchmarks: MPI Sintel [6], Bonn RGB-D [40], and ScanNet [9]. Table 2 compares our 4D generalist model against feed-forward 3D/4D geometry and pose specialists and diffusion depth specialists. Competitive Performance Against 3D/4D Specialists. Operating in just 8 NFE (number of denoising steps) without global alignment, on Sintel and ScanNet, WorldLatent14B outperforms diffusion baselines (DepthCrafter and Marigold-v1.1) and several established 3D/4D reconstruction specialists (DUSt3R, MASt3R, and MonST3R) in both depth and camera pose estimation. Notably, on the challenging dynamic MPI Sintel benchmark, WorldLatent-14B achieves the best δ1 depth accuracy (0.769) across all evaluated methods, surpassing even its feed-forward teacher DA3-Giant (0.763), Video-Depth-Anything-L (0.736), and VGGT-1B (0.705), while securing the second-best camera pose AUC@30 (0.701) and outperforming all video depth specialists in AbsRel (0.247). On ScanNet, our model ties DA3-Giant for the second-best AbsRel (0.042) with 0.978 δ1, and on Bonn it achieves the second-best camera pose AUC@30 (0.918) alongside 0.067 AbsRel and 0.961 δ1. As generalist 4D world model, WorldLatent performs comparably to state-of-the-art 4D perception specialists while uniquely supporting text-to-4D generation and controllable 4D re-rendering (D/P/G/R) from the same unified model. Figure 3 presents qualitative comparisons between our WorldLatent-14B and DA3-Giant across multiple datasets. 4.4. Fused 32-Channel WorldLatent vs. Naive 64-Channel Concatenation. In Table 4 (b), we ablate our DPT Fusion module against baseline that naively concatenates the four 16-channel modality latents along the channel dimension into 64-channel latent space (Separate 64-ch). Despite using half the latent channels (32 vs. 64), our Fused 32-ch representation achieves higher depth inlier accuracy (.777 vs. .768 δ1), lower ray direction error (5.03 vs. 5.90), lower temporal drift (.095 vs. .108), and substantial +9.3point improvement in camera pose AUC@30 (.692 vs. .599). This confirms that cross-modal DPT fusion eliminates inter-modality redundancy and enforces geometrickinematic coupling that makes the latent space significantly easier for the diffusion model to denoise. 5. Discussion We introduced WorldLatent, unified 4D latent representation protocol that bridges world perception and generative modeling. By fusing visual appearance, geometry, and camera dynamics into single compact WorldLatent bottleneck, our framework establishes shared spatial language across heterogeneous 4D tasks. Building on this, our Anyto-4D diffusion formulation consolidates perception, textto-4D generation, and controllable re-rendering into single generative model and optimization loop. Extensive exFigure 6. Linear subspace decomposition of WorldLatent. Visualization across videos re-rendered from an identical depth sequence under different text prompts (Row 1). The 16-D appearance projection Πz4d (Row 2) varies markedly with visual style, whereas the orthogonal 16-D geometry-and-camera projection Πz4d (Row 3) remains nearly invariant. Single-Loop Multi-Task Unification vs. Single-Task Specialists. We conduct controlled ablations using the Wan2.1T2V-1.3B backbone under an identical training budget to evaluate our multi-task formulation and unified latent bottleneck design  (Table 4)  . In Table 4(a), we compare our jointly trained unified model (J) against three separate single-task 1.3B specialists trained exclusively on perception (P), depth-conditioned rendering (R), or text-to-4D generation (G). While each specialist dedicates 100% of its capacity to single task and cannot execute the other tasks, our unified 1.3B checkpoint simultaneously handles all three task families with competitive performance across every metric (e.g., matching specialist in text alignment at .219 vs. .220 CLIP-T and .945 dynamic degree, and matching specialist at .960 vs. .964 render δ1). Moreover, as demonstrated in Tables 2 and 3, scaling the unified model from 1.3B to 14B parameters resolves this capacity bottle8 periments validate this unified approach, laying scalable blueprint toward general-purpose 4D spatial intelligence. While we have validated single-model 4D perception and generation at moderate scale, the effects of industrial-scale compute, parameters, and data remain unexplored. An open question for future large-scale research is whether scaling multi-task training over shared 4D latent space will catalyze emergent spatial and physical reasoning, analogous to the trajectory from GPT-2 [41] to modern frontier LLMs.

sections.content: A. Video Results B. More Training and Dataset Details . . B.1. Dataset Details . B.2. Training Details . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . C. Additional Visual Results . . C.1. Additional 4D Perception Visual Results C.2. Additional Re-rendering Results . . . . . C.3. Additional Text-based 4D Generation Results . . 13 13 13 13 14 14 14 14 A. Video Results Please refer to our project webpage for video results, which clearly demonstrate the effectiveness of our method and its comparison with baseline models. B. More Training and Dataset Details B.1. Dataset Details Multi-Domain Training Mixture. To train both WorldVAE (Stage 1) and our unified Any-to-4D diffusion model (Stage 2), we curate approximately 1.4M 17-frame video clips spanning 22 diverse data sources, summarized in Table 5. Our sampling distribution balances two complementary pools: Real-World Video Pool (79.4% of samples): Draws from large-scale open-domain and text-video corpora (SpatialVid-HQ [57], VidGen-1M [53], Kinetics600 [24], OpenVid-1M [39], Open-Sora [76]), cameraand object-centric real videos (RealCam-Vid [74], SAV [44], CO3D [45]), and egocentric or robotic manipulation streams (Ego-Exo4D [15], EgoDex [18], HOI4D [35], DROID [26]). This pool provides broad open-world visual concepts, complex non-rigid motion, realistic lighting, and diverse scene coverage essential for generalizable 4D generation and editing, with dense depth and camera pose pseudo-labels generated by DA3Giant [31]. Labeled 3D/4D Pool (20.6% of samples): Combines synthetic 4D datasets with exact rendering-engine depth and camera trajectories (PointOdyssey [75], OmniWorld [77], Hypersim [47], TartanAir [60], Dynamic Replica [23], VKITTI2 [7], MVS-Synth [20]) alongside calibrated real-sensor 3D scans (WildRGB-D [63], ScanNet++ [68], Waymo Open [50]). These datasets anchor sharp geometric boundaries, accurate occlusion disambiguation, and physically grounded 3D camera motion. 13 Because real-sensor 3D scans often contain sensor noise and incomplete depth regions, we likewise use DA3Giant [31] as teacher to generate clean, dense 4D labels for them. Across both pools, we use Gemini 3.5 Flash [54] to generate uniform, high-quality text captions for all video clips. Crucially, all zero-shot perception benchmarks evaluated in the main paper, MPI Sintel [6], Bonn RGB-D Dynamic [40], and ScanNet [9], as well as the 55 held-out clips used for generation evaluation, are strictly excluded from all Stage 1 and Stage 2 training splits. B.2. Training Details For WorldVAE (528M parameModel Parameters. ters), we initialize the four modality encoders and decoders from the Wan2.1-T2V VAE (4 127M), keeping the encoders frozen while fully fine-tuning the decoders alongside 20M-parameter DPT Fusion module. For Any-to-4D, we perform full-parameter fine-tuning of Wan2.1-T2V-14B (14B) for our final model and use Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B (1.3B) for controlled ablations. All models generate 17-frame 4D sequences at 512 512 resolution across RGB, depth, and Plucker ray maps. Training Details. We train our final 14B model on 256 TPU accelerators (32 GB memory each) for 108k steps with global batch size of 256. Optimization uses AdamW [36] (β2 = 0.95, weight decay 0) with learning rate of 3 105. During joint multi-task training, we sample tasks at each iteration with probabilities of 0.45 for textto-4D generation, 0.30 for depth-conditioned 4D editing/rerendering, and 0.25 for monocular 4D perception. During inference, we use Euler sampler [12, 33, 34] with flow shift 3. For Text-to-4D: we do 25 diffusion steps with Classifier Free Guidance (CFG) 4, CFG-rescale 0.7. For Render: we do 25 steps, with CFG 2. For Perception: we do 8 steps, with empty text, no guidance. For WorldVAE, we train with learning rate of 5 105. We set the reconstruction weights to λ1 = 4 (RGB), λ2 = 2 (depth), and λ3 = λ4 = 1 (Plucker ray maps), alongside λp = 1 (LPIPS), λg = 1 (depth gradient), λpts = 0.5 (3D pointmap), and λKL = 1 105. To support partialmodality conditioning in Stage 2, each training sample is encoded from randomly drawn modality subset (replacing omitted streams with learned mask token) with probabilities for inputs given to the encoder: 0.40 for all modalities (RGB + depth + rays), 0.20 for RGB only, 0.15 for depth only, 0.15 for rays only, 0.05 for RGB + depth, and 0.05 for RGB + rays. DPT Fusion module adapts DPT [43] to spatiotemporal latent fusion from scratch. Four 16-ch Wan2.1-VAE [55] latents (56464, patch size 1) receive learned modality embeddings and shared positional embeddings before entering 12-layer scratch ViT (d=192, 6 heads, 8.6M), where missing modalities use learned mask token. At four tap depths, the four modality tokens per cell are concatenated and MLP-fused, processed by zeroinitialized temporal mixers (2 temporal blocks/tap + 2 global cross-frame blocks, 7.2M), and aggregated via nonupsampling DPT pyramid (scales 1, 0.5, 0.25, 0.25, widths 48/96/192/384, 128-ch neck, 4.9M) into 64 channels (mean µ4d, and log-variance log σ2 4d) for the 32-ch z4d.
